analysis.title: GS U.S. Industrials & Materials | today + factors + AI EPS tomorrow
key_insights: Industrials were at session highs, up 150bps in line with broader markets, while materials were closer to flat. Technology and energy led the broader market and consumer staples fell the most.
Data center led the industrial subsectors and aerospace was also strong. Autos, airlines and agriculture lagged, with crude at its highs of the day weighing on oil-sensitive names.
Rates were holding at 4.99%. The dollar was at its highs and attempting a breakout, which the desk says is worth considering for exporters heading into 2027.

Desk inbounds from clients: CARR move after its presentation, KBR weakness (analyst day or the tape), where the appetite is in data center and which names investors return to, what to read into the CNM pre-announcement, LMT strength vs other primes, and FLY feedback.
The desk says factors and individual names tell different stories today, and asks whether the day is an unwind.

Momentum factor: today was the biggest outperformance of 12-month momentum vs shorter-term momentum, with both 3-month and 6-month momentum at records on GS data. Moves from AI and semis are now bleeding into 6-month momentum, which is selling off as recent losers rebound.
Three small-cap AI and data center names report on 11/12: FPS, LGN and DPC. All three went public within the last year and have been highly volatile.

FPS pre-announced positively in late October after a CFO change, with Q1 revenue and EBITDA at the higher end of or exceeding guidance. It peaked at $65 in June and may have bottomed at $18 in early November. A 3x+ book-to-bill is hard to sustain but lifts near-term estimates. It reports pre-market with a call at 11am.

LGN beat revenue by 10%+ in each of its four reported quarters, with EBITDA beats of 20%+. M&A has added to topline growth at reasonable multiples. It hit $100 in May and bottomed at $25 a few days ago, after going public in September 2025.

DPC reports pre-market on 11/12, its second report after a summer IPO. The stock rose 4% on the first report, and the options market implies a 13% move. It peaked above $55 in July and bottomed near $25 in late October. Watch comments on aerospace and IGT, and margins, which declined despite 30%+ revenue growth in Q2.
The desk is starting early conversations on 2027 themes, the macro setup and best idiosyncratic ideas.
Macro for the rest of the week: claims and existing home sales on 11/12 and PPI on 11/13.

Beat revenue by 10%+ and EBITDA by 20%+ in each of four reported quarters. Reports 11/12 and the desk will look for updates on M&A and 2027 given the backlog.

sector_views.rationale: The desk describes industrials at session highs, up 150bps, with data center and aerospace leading and autos, airlines and agriculture lagging. It gives no directional call.

earnings_insights: FPS (reports 11/12 pre-market, call at 11am): pre-announced in late October that fiscal Q1 revenue and EBITDA would be at the higher end of or exceed company guidance. This is company guidance, not a reported print. The desk cites a 3x+ book-to-bill.
LGN (reports 11/12): beat revenue by 10%+ in each of the four quarters reported so far and EBITDA by 20%+ (basis not specified).
DPC (reports 11/12 pre-market): second report as a public company. The stock rose 4% after the first report and the options-implied move is 13%. Q2 revenue growth was 30%+ with declining margins.
Other earnings: 11/12 pre-market AIRO, DPC, FPS, LGN, LUNR and post-market HAWK, SPCE, YSS. 11/13 pre-market LAC. 11/11 post-market AVEX, CAE, CTVA, TTEK.
